newsitem.title: CANADA: Hudson's eying Kmart, Eaton's stores.
newsitem.headline: Hudson's eying Kmart, Eaton's stores.

text.p: Hudson's Bay Co, Canada's largest department store retailer, said on Thursday that it was pursuing the acquisition of 36 stores from Kmart Canada and 10 Eaton's outlets.

Both Toronto-based chains have been seeking buyers for all or some of their outlets. Kmart Canada, wholly owned by Troy, Mich.-based Kmart Corp, has been trying to sell its 123-store chain since late 1995.
T Eaton Co Ltd, which is restructuring its Eaton's chain under court protection, has put 31 locations on the block.
Hudson's Bay spokesman Rob Moore said outgoing president George Kosich would seek approval from Hudson's Bay directors to put the offers together before his August retirement.
Moore could not provide any financial details for the possible transactions.
Kosich, 63, will be succeeded by former Wal-Mart Stores Inc executive Bill Fields, 47.
Toronto-based Hudson's Bay, which owns the upscale chain the Bay and discount retailer Zellers, would seek to turn the Kmart Canada and Eaton's outlets into Zellers stores, Moore said.

Hudson's Bay was seeking locations that complemented its Zellers sites, Wood Gundy analyst David Brodie said. "They're not going to go into markets where they have an existing Zellers store in the same mall or a mile away," he said.
Brodie said that if the acquisitions occurred, Hudson's Bay would be well positioned for the year-end holiday season, traditionally the most profitable time of year for retailers.
He added that the acquisitions would deepen Hudson's Bay debt, but that it could easily raise money from its banks.
Hudson's Bay had long-term debt of C$1.1 billion for fiscal 1997 ended January 31.
Brodie added that other Canadian or U.S.-based buyers might still step up to the plate for Kmart or Eaton's outlets.

Hudson's Bay also said today that it lost C$0.45 a share in its first quarter ended April 30 versus a year earlier loss of C$0.91 a share. The year ago loss included a restructuring charge of C$0.62 a share.
The latest loss exceeded analysts' expectations. Brodie had forecast a loss of C$0.30 a share and said he was on the "pessimistic" side of many predictions.
Hudson's Bay shares were down 0.30 to 28.20 on the Toronto Stock Exchange today.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109 or lydia.zajc@reuters.com))
